root_idea.summary: A single root principle of causing fright and driving away, together with fleeing and becoming distant in a scattered manner.
root_idea.development: The causative branch develops from flight and expulsion to dispersing others. In the Quranic use, treating one group in a conspicuous way makes it a deterrent that drives those who come after away.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic Form II verb is displayed under the normalized perfect-tense dictionary citation form شَرَّدَ rather than the attested imperative شَرِّدْ.

senses.definition: To disperse or scatter those who follow, causing them to flee.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction فَشَرِّدْ بِهِمْ مَنْ خَلْفَهُمْ, the group treated in this way becomes the means by which those behind are driven away and scattered.

senses.definition: To make a group notorious or terrifying as an example, so that others are deterred from similar opposition or conduct.
senses.usage_conditions: A deterrent or exemplary use of the construction with بِـ; the conspicuous treatment of one group warns and frightens those who come after them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an animal, to take fright or shy, flee or run away at random, become refractory, or break loose and go hither and thither.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of camels, horses, and similar animals; the meaning combines flight with unpredictable or refractory movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To depart, flee, go away or aside, or be driven away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person or other subject in expressions of going away from someone or withdrawing from a place; with عَلَى اللهِ, it can denote departing from obedience to God and separating from the faithful community.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone or an animal to take fright and flee, become refractory, or break loose; to drive away or expel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general transitive causative use, including driving a subject away from the speaker or from a place, apart from the specifically deterrent Quranic construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to be driven away or expelled, leaving him without a place of refuge, shelter, or lodging.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV causative construction concerning expulsion and the loss of a place of refuge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a people or party to go away or depart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form V use with a collective subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A taking fright or shying and fleeing or running away at random; a disposition to do so.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun or simple noun denoting either the act or the disposition associated with شَرَدَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One driven away or expelled; a fugitive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The fugitive sense is especially reported when the word occurs with طَرِيدٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who is alone or solitary.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct adjectival or substantive use of the same headword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A remainder or remnant of something, such as water, property, or livestock, deviating from the usual rule or pattern.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use for what remains apart from the main body or regular arrangement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an animal, taking fright or shying and fleeing or running away at random; refractory or prone to break loose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to male or female animals, especially camels, horses, and the like.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a rhyme, verse, or poem, circulating through lands, regions, cities, or towns.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use in the phrase قافية شاردة and related expressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a rhyme, verse, poem, word, or expression, strange, unusual, unfamiliar, or extraordinary; in lexicology, a barbarism.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative and technical use opposed to a fully idiomatic or eloquent expression.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers animal flight and human departure or withdrawal.
Contains the general causative meanings and the Quranic dispersal and deterrent uses.
Covers making someone notorious by exposing faults.
Covers expulsion without refuge or lodging.
Covers the intransitive departure of a people or party.
Covers the verbal noun or noun denoting flight and a disposition to flee.
Covers the expelled or fugitive person and the distinct sense of one who is solitary.
Covers a remainder or remnant deviating from the regular body.
Covers the active-participle description of a frightened or refractory animal.
Covers the figurative use for a rhyme, verse, or poem circulating through regions.
Covers strange or extraordinary poetic and lexical expressions.

cautions: The single Quranic occurrence is the imperative شَرِّدْ. Its closely related lexical readings include dispersing or scattering, terrifying, and making a group notorious as a deterrent; these are represented as two Quranic senses rather than treating the contextual gloss alone as a separate meaning.
